newsitem.title: FRANCE: French crime rate dips for second year.
newsitem.headline: French crime rate dips for second year.

text.p: The crime rate in France fell for the second year in a row in 1996, Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre said on Wednesday.
The number of registered crimes and offences fell 2.88 percent from 1995.
"Over two years, there has been a fall of almost 10 percent in crime in France," Debre told a news conference. "Today crime is back to a level below that of 1991."
While hailing the fall, he said he was worried by rising crime among the young and a high level of offences linked to drugs.

The centre-right government has sought to stiffen sanctions while a heightened police presence in many cities after a wave of bombings by Algerian extremists in 1995 that killed eight people may have discouraged crime.
